prov.heading: Allowance for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The allowance for credit losses has been determined in accordance with GAAP. The Company is responsible for the timely and periodic determination of the amount of the allowance for credit losses. Management believes that the allowance for credit losses is adequate to cover expected credit losses over the life of the loan portfolio. Although management evaluates available information to determine the adequacy of the allowance for credit losses, the level of allowance is an estimate which is subject to significant judgment and short-term change. Because of uncertainties associated with local and national economic forecasts, the operating and regulatory environment, collateral values and future cash flows from the loan portfolio, it is possible that a material change could occur in the allowance for credit losses in the near term. The evaluation of the adequacy of loan collateral is often based upon estimates and appraisals. Because of changing economic conditions, the valuations determined from such estimates and appraisals may also change.

Accordingly, the Company may ultimately incur losses that vary from management’s current estimates. Adjustments to the allowance for credit losses will be reported in the period in which such adjustments become known and can be reasonably estimated.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
Noninterest expenses consist primarily of salaries and employee benefits, building occupancy and equipment expenses, advertising and promotion expenses, data processing expenses, legal and professional services and miscellaneous other operating expenses.

The following table sets forth the principal components of noninterest expense for the periods indicated (amounts in thousands).

Noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $19.9 million compared with $18.1 million for the same period of 2025. The overall increase was primarily a result of the increase in salaries and employee benefits coinciding with growth in the number of employees. Salaries and employee benefits increased $1.6 million, or 14.17%, to $12.9 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $11.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $58.6 million compared with $52.3 million for the same period of 2025. The overall increase was primarily a result of the increase in salaries and employee benefits coinciding with growth in the number of employees that was offset by the decrease in legal and other professional services. Legal and other professional services decreased $1.1 million, or 50.96%, to $1.0 million in the first nine months of 2026 from $2.1 million in the first nine months of 2025.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text:
We recognized income tax expense of $4.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was 24.3% compared to 21.4% for the same period in 2025. The effective tax rate is affected by levels of items of income that are not subject to federal and/or state taxation and by levels of items of expense that are not deductible for federal and/or state income tax purposes.

We recognized income tax expense of $13.7 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $9.0 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was 24.1% compared to 22.4% for the same period in 2025. The effective tax rate is affected by levels of items of income that are not subject to federal and/or state taxation and by levels of items of expense that are not deductible for federal and/or state income tax purposes.

net.heading: Net Income
net.text: During the three months ended September 30, 2026, our net income was $15.0 million, compared to $10.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $4.4 million, or 41.02%. The primary reason for the increase in net income for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to the third quarter of 2025 was an increase in net interest income. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income was $36.4 million compared to $31.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $5.0 million, or 15.95%. This increase is a result of loan growth and higher yields on new and repricing loans. Total noninterest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $5.4 million compared to $2.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The most significant increases were attributable to the $361.0 thousand and $375.0 thousand increase in service charges and fees and secondary market mortgage operations, respectively, combined with a $2.9 million decrease in net losses on sales of investment securities. Total noninterest expense in the third quarter of 2026 increased $1.8 million, or 9.79%, from the third quarter of 2025.

Net interest income.text: Net interest income increase of $5.0 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, representing a 15.95% rate of increase over the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
In addition to net interest income, we generate various types of noninterest income from our operations. Our banking operations generate revenue from service charges and fees mainly on deposit accounts. Our mortgage division generates revenue from originating and selling mortgage loans. Our investment brokerage division generates revenue through a revenue-sharing relationship with a registered broker-dealer. We also own life insurance policies on several key employees and record income on the increase in the cash surrender value of these policies.

The following table sets forth the principal components of noninterest income for the periods indicated (amounts in thousands).

Noninterest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $5.4 million compared to $2.0 million for the same period in 2025. The most significant increase in noninterest income was the result of the loss on sales of investment securities which totaled $614.0 thousand in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the loss on sales of investment securities which totaled $3.5 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $17.3 million compared to $9.0 million for the same period in 2025.

intro.text: We are a bank holding company headquartered in Prattville, Alabama. River Bank & Trust was formed as an Alabama banking corporation in March 2006. In November 2012, River Financial Corporation was formed as an Alabama corporation and all the common shares of River Bank & Trust were exchanged for common shares of River Financial Corporation and River Bank & Trust became the wholly owned subsidiary of River Financial Corporation. We operate one subsidiary bank, River Bank & Trust. Through the Bank, we provide a broad array of financial services to businesses, business owners, and professionals. We operate 23 full-service banking offices, located in Montgomery, Prattville, Millbrook, Wetumpka, Auburn, Opelika, Alexander City, Dothan, Enterprise, Daphne, Clanton, Mobile, Gadsden, Decatur, Saraland, Huntsville, Birmingham, and Florence, Alabama.
